components.name: Approval gate
components.description: Human-Gate or Agent-Gate. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.4. One kind, two modes; they differ only in who decides. reviewer: human parks the run as waiting_human. reviewer: agent is a machine check whose verdict is {pass, reason}; today that check is an LLM judge. mode: check is RESERVED and refused. A human gate is optional. Without a key the agent-gate does not wave anything through — it escalates to a human.

escalateOn.notes: objection hands a failed check to a person. Default objection.

status.notes: reviewer: human — the run is waiting_human until qloop approve continues it or --reject fails it.

components.name: Telegram publish
components.description: A named recipe over api-request, not a new engine kind. POSTs to Telegram sendMessage with {{env.TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN}} and {{env.TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID}}. The runner still executes api-request (SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.3). Unset env vars do not fire a URL with braces in it — the runner writes to .qf/out/ and says so (SPEC §9).

text.notes: Message body. In shipped loops this is a prior step's output, templated into api-request body.

sent.notes: Recipe surface, not an engine field. True when the api-request completed; false when the file sink was used instead.

chatId.notes: Optional. The chat that was addressed. Not an engine field — the request body carries chat_id.

builtins.name: API request
builtins.description: An outgoing request. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.3. Without body, the last successful output is sent in an envelope {runId, templateId, payload}. A loop may end here. This is a complete loop, not an unfinished one. SPEC does not enumerate response fields.

body.notes: JSON string or text. templated, deeply.

response.notes: SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.3 does not list output fields. The step performs the request; when it is last, the loop is complete.

builtins.name: Fan-out
builtins.description: A lane per item. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.5. over must be exactly one placeholder resolving to an ARRAY. Mixed text returns nothing rather than guessing. If it does not resolve to an array, the step fails and says why. Each lane step sees its own item through {{item.…}} and {{index}}. Truncation is never silent. Without over, the lane is inlined and runs once, and the node says so rather than pretending to expand.

over.notes: a single template resolving to an ARRAY, e.g. {{steps.Fetch feed.output.entries}}.

itemsFound.notes: How many items the source held.

itemsTaken.notes: How many lanes were opened after the cap.

truncated.notes: A note when the cap cut the list. Never silent.

builtins.name: Fetch
builtins.description: Read a source. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.1. Fails on non-2xx, on a network error, and — for format: rss — on a feed with no items. An empty feed is not a success: the steps after it expect material. The RSS reader is regex-based, not an XML parser.

status.notes: HTTP status. Present on every format.

count.notes: format: rss — number of entries kept.

entries.notes: format: rss — each entry is {title, link, summary, published}.

builtins.name: Schedule
builtins.description: A trigger, not a runner step. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §5.6 / §3: triggers are inputs, not steps; they never appear in steps:. The runner does not act on any trigger. qloop run performs one pass; cron: documents the intended cadence, and launchd or cron actually fires it.

cron.notes: 5 fields, UTC. Checked: field count and ranges. SPEC-MANIFEST.md §3.

none.notes: Not a step. No runner output. Placing schedule in steps: is a validation error.
